title: Traffic-clustered exemplar selection for quantization calibration packs
creator: Aisha Raman
description: Objective: produce reproducible, per-domain calibration packs for FP8 and INT8 quantization that (1) capture the distribution of production prompts, (2) prioritize high-impact traffic slices, and (3) minimize calibration-induced accuracy regressions. This ticket defines the sampling algorithm, curation heuristics, validation criteria, and rollout plan for shipping 'traffic-clustered' exemplar packs to the calibration pipeline. Rationale: existing stratified packs underrepresent bursty, low-frequency-but-high-value queries and do not weight clusters by live traffic patterns, which leads to calibration drift for certain enterprise domains. Approach blends embedding-clustering, perplexity stratification, and decayed reservoir sampling to produce compact packs per domain.
success_criteria: Per-domain FP8/INT8 calibration packs produced and consumed by calibrator; validation against holdout set shows - mean token-level KL divergence <= 0.015 vs baseline (FP16) AND top-1 human acceptability delta <= 1.5% across monitored domains. Packs must be <= 5k examples per domain for Dedicated customers and <= 2k for hosted test runs.
sampling_algorithm: 1) For each domain, collect N most recent 90 days of prompts (N configurable; default 500k). 2) Compute 512-d embeddings (prod embedding model) and normalized token-length, and compute per-prompt perplexity relative to current FP16 production model. 3) Run k-means on embeddings with k = min(50, sqrt(domain_unique_user_count)). 4) Within each cluster, stratify by perplexity buckets (low/medium/high) and response-length bins (short/medium/long). 5) Score examples by traffic_weight * cluster_representativeness_score * novelty_score. traffic_weight = decay_weighted_request_count(last 30d, half-life=7d). novelty_score boosts rare lexical patterns (TF-IDF tail). 6) Use decayed reservoir sampling to pick up to domain_cap per cluster; enforce minimum coverage floor so each cluster contributes at least 1% of pack unless domain too small. 7) Deduplicate by normalized prompt text + deterministic fingerprint; prefer latest example for identical fingerprints. 8) Produce separate FP8 and INT8 candidate packs with identical sampling but different tokenization checks and model-probing annotations.
curation_rules: - Dedup threshold: Jaccard token overlap > 0.95 -> collapse. - Exclude PII using regex + KMS-enabled PII scanning pipeline; flagged examples go to 'sensitive' bucket for manual review. - Include at least 3% adversarial/generated examples (from synthetic fuzz tests) per domain to preserve robustness. - Cap per-customer examples to 2% of domain pack to protect privacy. - Ensure distributional parity across weekdays/weekends and hour-of-day when domain traffic is highly cyclical.
validation_plan: 1) Split out a holdout set (20%) stratified by cluster and perplexity. 2) Run calibrations for FP8 and INT8 on the training portion; evaluate on holdout for metrics: token-level KL, per-token perplexity delta, response-level BLEU/ROUGE-ish similarity (where applicable), hallucination rate (automated heuristics), and downstream acceptance (A/B human eval on 1k samples per domain). 3) Repeat calibration with 5 random seeds to measure variance. 4) Signal fail when any domain shows KL > 0.03 OR human acceptability drop > 3% OR hallucination increase > 2x. 5) Produces validation report and artifacts: calibration logs, model diffs, token-distribution histograms, and failing examples CSV.
instrumentation_and_dashboards: - New console dashboard: 'Calibration Packs -> Domain X' showing cluster distribution, traffic-weighted coverage, candidate vs holdout metrics. - Traceability: each exemplar annotated with origin (customer_id_hash or public), timestamp, cluster_id, perplexity_score, and sampling_score. - Alerting: daily drift monitor when new pack token-distribution JS divergence > 0.02 vs previous pack. - Links to dashboards: https://console.redwood.ai/dash/calibration-packs (placeholder).
rollout_plan: Stage 1: internal cal pipeline runs on new packs for a small set of non-sensitive domains (week 0-2). Stage 2: canary to dedicated clusters for 3 customers per domain with shadow routing and cost/latency monitoring (week 2-4). Stage 3: widen to all dedicated customers and limited hosted test runs if validation passes (week 4-8). Rollback: automatic fallback to FP16/previous quant-profile on SLA/quality breach. SRE playbook updated with rollback runbook and KPIs.
risks_and_mitigation: - Risk: Overfitting to recent traffic -> Mitigate by time-decay and enforced older-sample fraction (min 15%). - Risk: PII leakage -> Mitigate by strong PII filters and manual review pipeline for flagged examples. - Risk: Undercoverage of long-tail intents -> Mitigate via novelty_score and per-cluster floors. - Risk: Calibration instability across seeds -> Mitigate by ensemble calibration runs and adopting the most conservative weight schedule.
open_questions: - What is the canonical embedding model and refresh cadence? (proposal: embed-prod-v2, refresh quarterly). - Should the packs include user metadata buckets (browser/agent) to detect UI-driven prompts? Privacy impact pending. - Acceptance thresholds: can PM relax KL target for latency-sensitive tenants? (PM input needed).
